notes: The interface can now be built as an Android app: npm run android:apk, once npx cap add android has been run.
The app asks once for the shop's server address, checks it really answers, and remembers it.
The database address and token stay on the server and never travel inside the app — an APK is a zip file anyone can read.
render.yaml now deploys against the hosted database instead of a disk, because a file on one server cannot be shared with a phone.
Existing browser and desktop installations are unchanged: with no address configured the app talks to its own origin exactly as before.
The phone is a device the account has not used, so the first sign-in on it asks for the emailed code — then remembers it for 30 days.
No offline support on the phone. No signal means no sales, the same as the hosted desktop.
